headline: ASX closes up 0.33% but your AI and energy ETFs took the biggest hits today — GXAI dropped 4.6% as rate-cut chatter dominates Aussie headlines.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Biggest mover in your portfolio today, down 4.6% to $17.01. AI-focused ETFs have been volatile globally as investors weigh up new US government rules that could slow how quickly companies like Google and OpenAI can launch new models. The ETF is now down 10.6% from what you paid for it — still in the red, but the underlying AI story remains intact.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Fell 1.96% to $8.52 today despite crude oil prices being essentially flat (WTI oil at $88.24, barely changed). The move looks like broader profit-taking on energy stocks rather than any big supply-side news. The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) actually warned this week that global oil inventories are heading toward multi-decade lows, which should be a longer-term positive for energy companies.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Dropped another 1.71% to $5.76, and is now 14.5% below what you paid. Lithium stocks have been in a tough spot as the market wrestles with whether the next price recovery is weeks or months away. There are some positive signs — Scotiabank flagged this week that demand is building and low production costs support a recovery — but sentiment remains cautious.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Slipped 0.97% to $91.11 today. Emerging markets are feeling a slight headwind from the Aussie dollar softening (down 0.35% against the USD to $0.7016), which paradoxically can cut into AUD-denominated returns on globally exposed ETFs. Nothing alarming — just a quiet drift lower.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Edged down 0.31% to $516.50 today. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, so it moves with US sentiment from the previous night's session. No major news driving the dip — just mild softness flowing through. Still essentially flat on your cost base overall.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Barely moved — down just 0.08% to $75.28. VDHG is diversified across global and Aussie shares, so the small individual moves across markets mostly cancelled each other out today. Rock steady.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: US markets haven't opened yet tonight, so last night's close of $361.17 is the most recent price. Alphabet's story remains solid — analysts are pointing to a massive cloud backlog and dominant search ad cash flow as reasons to stay positive even amid the AI spending debate. Apple is also reportedly partnering with Google on its most advanced AI model, which is a useful revenue channel for Alphabet.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Last night's close was $411.74 — US markets open later tonight. Microsoft continues to ride the AI wave, with analysts noting strong earnings momentum and cloud growth. The AI boom narrative remains firmly behind this one.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Last close $212.55, US markets yet to open tonight. Fresh speculation is circulating that a GTA 6 Trailer 3 could drop very soon, with gaming media citing new evidence. Any trailer release tends to spike TTWO's share price — one to watch closely this week.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Big drop today — hold your nerve
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 4.6% today to $17.01, now down 10.6% overall on your cost base. The sell-off is linked to new US government rules potentially slowing AI model launches from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic. The underlying AI growth story hasn't changed, but sentiment is shaky short-term. No reason to sell into panic — hold.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 Trailer 3 could drop any day
watch_today.detail: Gaming media is reporting fresh evidence that Rockstar/Take-Two could release GTA 6 Trailer 3 very soon. Previous trailers caused TTWO's stock to spike sharply. If you've been thinking about adding to this position, watch for the announcement — a trailer drop is likely to move the price fast. Current last close: $212.55 USD.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium still soft — patience required
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped another 1.71% today to $5.76, sitting 14.5% below your cost base. The lithium market is in a tug-of-war between recovering demand signals and policy headwinds from overseas. Scotiabank is cautiously positive on the sector, but there's no clear catalyst for a sharp rebound yet. Hold — selling now locks in the loss.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cuts: the big Aussie story this week
watch_today.detail: Multiple banks and economists are now calling for the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) to cut interest rates, with NAB updating its forecast to include a cut. One economist warned the RBA risks triggering a recession if it doesn't act. Rate cuts are generally good for growth stocks and ETFs like VDHG — keep an eye on any RBA communication this week.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: EIA warns of multi-decade low oil inventories
watch_today.detail: The US Energy Information Administration warned this week that global crude oil stockpiles are falling toward their lowest levels in decades, which should support elevated oil prices through 2026. This is a medium-term positive for your energy ETF (FUEL.AX), even though it dipped 1.96% today. Hold — the fundamental backdrop is supportive.

watch_today.title: Apple + Google AI partnership — good for GOOG
watch_today.detail: Apple announced it's partnering with Google (and Nvidia) to power its most advanced AI model. This is a meaningful revenue opportunity for Alphabet — being Apple's AI partner gives Google distribution across hundreds of millions of iPhones. A quiet positive for your GOOG holding.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 finished up 0.33% today to 8,653, a quiet positive session despite weakness in some tech and energy names. Gold took a meaningful tumble — down 1.73% to $4,186 USD/oz — suggesting some risk appetite returning as investors moved out of safe-haven assets. Crude oil is flat at $88.24. The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to 70.16 US cents. US markets (S&P 500 last at 7,405 and NASDAQ at 25,929) haven't opened yet tonight — check back tomorrow morning for overnight moves.

politics.summary: Aussie rate cuts are dominating the financial-political conversation today, with major banks and economists pushing hard for the RBA to act. The debate is heating up — cut too late and risk recession, cut now and risk being seen as premature.

stories.title: NAB updates forecast, now expects an RBA interest rate cut
stories.why_it_matters: NAB has revised its forecasts and now officially expects the RBA to cut interest rates. This is significant because NAB is one of Australia's Big Four banks — when they shift their view, markets pay attention. Lower interest rates generally mean cheaper mortgages and a boost to growth assets like shares and property. Good news for ETF holders like you.

stories.title: Reserve Bank warned it must cut rates or risk triggering a recession
stories.why_it_matters: Economists are now warning the RBA that sitting on its hands too long could tip Australia into recession — a technical recession means two consecutive quarters of shrinking economic output. The concern is that high interest rates are squeezing household budgets hard enough to choke consumer spending. If the RBA doesn't cut soon, the economic slowdown could become self-reinforcing.

stories.title: Why the RBA may not be able to cut even if Australia falls into recession
stories.why_it_matters: A counterpoint piece in the West Australian argues that even if Australia tips into recession, the RBA might not be able to cut rates because inflation could still be running too hot. This is the central bank's dilemma: inflation requires high rates, but a weak economy needs low ones. If the RBA is stuck, mortgage holders and investors may be waiting longer than the market currently hopes.

stories.title: One of Australia's biggest banks says interest rate pain is over — for now
stories.why_it_matters: One of Australia's major banks is telling customers the worst of the rate hike cycle is behind us — the repeated increases to the cash rate that pushed mortgage repayments sharply higher appear to be done. The caveat is 'for now', suggesting rates may stay on hold for a while before any cuts arrive. For borrowers and property investors, this is cautious relief.

ai.summary: It's a big week for AI news — Anthropic dropped two new Claude models, Apple completely rebuilt Siri with AI, and the US government is moving toward new rules that could reshape how AI companies operate. Lots happening that's directly relevant to your holdings.

stories.title: Apple launches all-new 'Siri AI' — a completely rebuilt personal assistant
stories.why_it_matters: Apple has officially announced a ground-up rebuild of Siri, calling it 'Siri AI' and describing it as 'profoundly more capable and personal'. This isn't just a tweak — it's a complete overhaul. Apple is also partnering with Google and Nvidia to power its most advanced AI model, meaning your GOOG holding benefits from being baked into Apple's AI stack across hundreds of millions of devices.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 to the public
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic has publicly released two new models — Claude Fable 5 (a lighter, faster model) and Claude Mythos 5 (the heavy-duty one that reportedly rocked Wall Street when it was privately previewed two months ago). Mythos 5 is now available to everyone, not just enterprise customers. These are now available on Snowflake's Cortex AI platform as well, meaning business adoption will accelerate quickly. This raises the competitive bar for Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot.

stories.title: Trump signs new AI executive order that could change how OpenAI, Google and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has signed a new AI executive order that would change the process for how companies like OpenAI, Google and Anthropic release new AI models. The order is expected to introduce new compliance and oversight requirements before launching powerful models publicly. This adds regulatory friction (new rules and approval steps) for the big AI players — potentially slowing the pace of releases and adding costs. This is the likely reason GXAI.AX sold off today.

stories.title: Australia's AI regulation heading for crucial review
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's approach to regulating artificial intelligence is about to undergo a significant review process. The outcome will determine what guardrails local businesses — and global AI companies operating here — will need to follow. For Australian investors in AI-exposed ETFs like GXAI.AX, this could affect how quickly AI gets adopted in Australia and what compliance costs local tech companies face.

sport.summary: NRL Round 15 kicks off tomorrow night with Rabbitohs vs Broncos, and there's big AFL news with Gary Ablett inducted into the Hall of Fame and a mid-game medical scare. Nick Kyrgios is also making noise at a major tennis tournament.

stories.title: Round 15 NRL team lists confirmed — Latrell Mitchell update from Wayne Bennett
stories.why_it_matters: Round 15 kicks off tomorrow night with Rabbitohs vs Broncos at Accor Stadium (7:50pm). Wayne Bennett has given an update on Latrell Mitchell ahead of the game, and there's also a reveal about a debutant. Fox Sports is also flagging 'long term concerns for the Broncos' — worth watching given they're in tomorrow's opener. The Dolphins host the Roosters at Suncorp on Friday night.

stories.title: Gary Ablett inducted into AFL Hall of Fame — teammates react
stories.why_it_matters: AFL legend Gary Ablett has officially been inducted into the AFL Hall of Fame, with teammates paying tribute to one of the greatest players of the modern era. The announcement came during what's been a big week for the AFL — the competition also reported record crowds and viewership for Round 13, showing the code is in rude health.

stories.title: AFL game halted as star rushed to hospital
stories.why_it_matters: An AFL match was stopped mid-game after a player was rushed to hospital. No article text available on the specific player or condition, but the incident was significant enough to halt play entirely.

stories.title: Kyrgios 'emotional' after ousting a seeded player in stunning comeback win
stories.why_it_matters: Nick Kyrgios has knocked out a seeded player in what's being described as a sizzling comeback win, and was visibly emotional afterwards. Kyrgios's return to competitive tennis has been one of the feel-good stories of 2026 — he's clearly firing again. No specific tournament details in the available article text, but the win over a seed is a significant result.
